{{Quote|Pull up the charts and pick one, then. Like I said, the Javin's got plenty of places to hide&hellip;|Solomahal, to [[Covah]]|<ref name="GG" />}}
The '''Lutrillians''' were [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] indigenous to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Lutrillia/Legends|Lutrillia]], in the [[Yarith sector/Legends|Yarith sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. Members of the [[Species/Legends|species]] had broad, wrinkled features, pointed [[Ear/Legends|ears]], and hair growing from their heads and cheeks. Thick skin and a layer of [[blubber]] bolstered them against physical damage and harsh cold. The Lutrillians evolved a [[nomad]]ic lifestyle to avoid subterranean predators and to visit oases scattered about their remarkably flat [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]]. They adapted to the introduction of [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] technology by moving into wheeled [[City/Legends|platform-cities]]. These mechanical beasts lumbered across the planet's equator, stripping the surface of food, [[Water/Legends|water]], and raw materials. Lutrillians enjoyed adventure, high stakes, and chance-taking, traits that made them natural entrepreneurs.

In the early [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of their world's introduction to the greater galaxy, traveling to Lutrillia required a time-consuming side trip from the [[Corellian Trade Spine/Legends|Corellian Trade Spine]] in what was then considered [[Javin sector/Legends|Mugaari Space]]. Around [[400 BBY/Legends|400 BBY]], the [[Scout/Legends|explorer]] and entrepreneur [[Ecclessis Figg/Legends|Ecclessis Figg]] blazed a more direct route to the world that became known as the [[Lutrillian Cross/Legends|Lutrillian Cross]]. The Lutrillians found themselves with greater contact to the outside galaxy than ever before, and their influence in the [[Greater Javin/Legends|Greater Javin]] region of the Outer Rim expanded. Lutrillians established themselves on many worlds. Some of the more successful Lutrillians included [[Solomahal/Legends|Solomahal]], a [[General/Legends|general]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], [[Treva Horme]], head salesbeing and executive planner for [[Planet Dreams, Incorporated|Planet Dreams, Inc.]], on [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]], and [[Sawthawne]], a [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] of that same world.

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:LutrillianChild-MaraJadeByTheEmperorsHand2.png|thumb|left|250px|Some Lutrillians, such as this juvenile on Svivren, had three-fingered hands.]]
Lutrillians were [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] bipeds who stood between 1.5 and 2 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in height. Thick skin<ref name="GATORW" />&mdash;in shades that varied from white<ref name="A" /> or pale<ref name="TSWHS" /> to red<ref name="Dec" /> or tan&mdash;protected them from damage, and a deep [[Blubber|layer of fat]] kept them insulated from frigid temperatures. Some Lutrillians had sharp, claw-like fingernails,<ref name="GATORW" /> while others had blunt nails like a [[Human/Legends|Human]];<ref name="TSWHS" /> similar variation marked the number of digits, with Lutrillians having three, four, or five fingers per hand.<ref name="TSWHS" /><ref name="MJ2" /><ref name="GATORW" /><ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|II|58|Horme, Treva}}</ref>

Their faces were broad and wrinkled, with big, cleft mouths, wide, flat noses, and large, wide-set, brown,<ref name="GATORW" /> black,<ref name="TSWHS" /> or pink<ref name="A" /> [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] with heavy lids.<ref name="TSWHS" /><ref name="SOTJ">[[Secrets of the Jedi (novel)|''Secrets of the Jedi'']]</ref> In some specimens, pink lips bordered the wide mouth, which in turn held white [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]].<ref name="Dec" /> Their pointed ears stuck straight up from the sides of their heads. Thick gray or brown hair grew from their heads and jowls.<ref name="MJ2" /><ref name="TSWHS" /> Their facial furrows deepened and changed depending on their emotional state.<ref name="SOTJ" /> Lutrillians entered adolescence at thirteen standard [[Standard year/Legends|years]] and were considered full adults at eighteen standard years. The average life expectancy for members of the [[Species/Legends|species]] was ninety standard years.<ref name="GATORW" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|You are too cautious, Commander Kenobi. I think we can win this.|Solomahal, to Obi-Wan Kenobi, during the Battle of Azure Spaceport|<ref name="SOTJ" />}}
Lutrillians were astute and clever with an inclination toward adventure and nomadism. They were natural risk-takers, a penchant that manifested even more strongly when personal gain&mdash;especially [[Currency/Legends|monetary]] gain&mdash;was at stake. This combination of greed and risk made them gifted entrepreneurs and hagglers. Other races generally found the Lutrillians to be friendly and easy to get along with, although the Lutrillians' experience living in overcrowded conditions made them a bit clueless as to what other beings considered personal space.<ref name="GATORW" /> Lutrillians got along well with their galactic neighbors, including various Human and [[Nothoiin (species)/Legends|Nothoiin]] populations. Nevertheless, the [[Mugaari]] species viewed the Lutrillians as collaborators for failing to resist the Human "invaders" who had "conquered" the region.<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>

[[File:Treva-horme.jpg|thumb|left|280px|Lutrillians like Treva Horme often excelled in business.]]
On their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], [[Lutrillia/Legends|Lutrillia]], the Lutrillians inhabited enormous wheeled [[City/Legends|platform-cities]] that barreled across the tundra. At any one time, there were about 100 such contraptions roaming the [[Planet/Legends|planet's]] equatorial regions, half headed east and the rest west, pausing only to gather supplies such as food, [[Water/Legends|water]], and raw materials from the surface.<ref name="GATORW" /> Smaller and faster [[Transport/Legends|transports]] ferried passengers and cargo between the giants. While the species had access to all aspects of [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] technology, the cities were too small to accommodate the world's 800 million Lutrillians comfortably, so conditions were often overcrowded.<ref name="GG" /><ref name="GATORW" /> Each city was governed by an independent city council.<ref name="GG" />

The Lutrillians' primary export was [[ochroid dust]]. They imported high technology, especially mechanical parts to keep up and improve their wheeled cities&mdash;even these behemoth biomes could fall prey to the world's burrowing predators should they break down.<ref name="GG" /> The Lutrillians spoke a rough-edged language, also known as [[Lutrillian (language)|Lutrillian]], that was replete with short grunts and snorts. Most Lutrillians could understand and speak [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]]. Some Lutrillian names were Atheloe, Erathewen, Flewel, Hwarrthi, and Luthinoe.<ref name="GATORW" />

==History==
===Early Lutrillian history===
[[File:Lutrillian_Cross_and_Kiax_Nebula.jpg|thumb|right|270px|The blazing of the Lutrillian Cross hyperlane around 400 BBY connected the Lutrillians to the rest of the Greater Javin.]]
The Lutrillians evolved on Lutrillia in the [[Lutrillia system/Legends|Lutrillia system]],<ref name="TEA" /> part of the [[Greater Javin/Legends|Greater Javin]] region of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]].<ref name="GG" /> Lutrillia was a cold, inhospitable place. The primary terrain was endless expanses of flat, dry, tundra criss-crossed by frozen rivers.<ref name="GATORW" /> Scarce oases of fresh liquid water dotted the world's equator.<ref name="GATORW " /> As the Lutrillians developed intelligence, they took to wandering between these water sources, ever watchful for burrowing predators such as [[chomper]]s and [[nipper]]s.<ref name="GG" />

[[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] [[Scout/Legends|scouts]] made contact with the Lutrillians sometime between [[3000 BBY|3000]] and [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]]. Although the world briefly became part of territory controlled by the [[New Sith]] Empire during the latter phase of the [[New Sith Wars]] of [[1004 BBY|1004]] to 1000 BBY, around this time, Lutrillia lay beyond the Republic outpost world of [[Javin]] at the end of the [[Corellian Trade Spine/Legends|Corellian Trade Spine]] and the edge of the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] in what was then considered [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]].<ref name="TEA" /> [[Kiax Nebula/Legends|Kiax]], the spinward half of the hazardous [[Twin Nebulae/Legends|Twin Nebulae]] nearby, prevented a direct [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] to the world. A detour passed through Mugaari Space, where the native Mugaari demanded a hefty portion of any profits from [[Merchant/Legends|traders]] heading to Lutrillia. As a result, contact between the Lutrillians and outsiders was rare,<ref name="GG" /> but intrepid traders did find it worthwhile to navigate the hazards of Mugaari Space and tolerate the slow route to trade with the Lutrillians.<ref name="TEA" /> Efforts to find a more direct route to their world failed. The Republic's subsequent defeat of the Mugaari in a brief war and the annexation of their territory made Lutrillia part of the [[Javin sector/Legends|Javin sector]] but otherwise had little effect on their economic and [[Politics/Legends|political]] realities.<ref name="GG" />

Around [[400 BBY/Legends|400 BBY]],<ref name="400 BBY">"[[Galactic Gazetteer: Hoth and the Greater Javin]]," which is set during the Rebellion and New Republic eras ([[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]]&ndash;[[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]]; see {{Blog|holocron|24|Star Wars Eras}}), states that the [[Anoat sector/Legends|Anoat sector]] was established in the last [[Standard year/Legends|year]] of [[Ecclessis Figg/Legends|Ecclessis Figg's]] life. The text states that Figg [[Death/Legends|died]] nearly four [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]] prior to its setting, thus providing an approximate date of [[400 BBY/Legends|400 BBY]] for the Anoat [[Sector/Legends|sector's]] establishment.</ref> the explorer [[Ecclessis Figg/Legends|Ecclessis Figg]] launched an expedition from [[Gerrenthum/Legends|Gerrenthum]] to map the unknown regions adjacent to the [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] Trade Spine. He was rewarded with a direct route to Lutrillia that cut through the Twin Nebulae and on to the ancient, roundabout route to Lutrillia from the Mid Rim. The route became known as the [[Lutrillian Cross/Legends|Lutrillian Cross]],<ref name="GG" /> and its continuation west to [[Koda Space Station]] along the [[Koda Spur/Legends|Koda Spur]].<ref name="TEA" />

===Contact and exploration===
[[File:Solomahal_from_Jedi_Knights_TCG.png|thumb|left|270px|Solomahal served as a Republic general in the Clone Wars and later went into hiding on Tatooine.]]
Contact between Lutrillians and outsiders blossomed, and Republic investment and trade infused Lutrillia and the region around the Twin Nebulae with new life. Figg was careful to avoid conflict by keeping this arrangement beneficial to all involved, and the influx of capital and high technology caused a paradigm shift on the world. The Lutrillians used their newfound wealth and technology to create vast, wheeled cities. They continued to roam their world as they had for generations, only now, they were afforded greater speed and protection from burrowing predators.<ref name="GG" />

Over the next few decades, Figg's company of explorers blazed new hyperlanes through the region, and the Lutrillians found themselves more and more connected to the greater galaxy. The species established colonies on nearby worlds such as [[Kirtarkin/Legends|Kirtarkin]], Gerrenthum, and [[Ione/Legends|Ione]], and Lutrillian businessbeings set up operations across the region. For example, Lutrillian investors set up [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceports]] on the swamp world [[Mijos/Legends|Mijos]], although many of their structures sank into mud due to poor design. Their region's influence grew such that the Republic demarcated a new [[Anoat sector/Legends|Anoat subsector]] in the area, and later split it into the Anoat and [[Yarith sector/Legends|Yarith]] [[Sector/Legends|sectors]]. Worlds with significant Lutrillian populations were divided between the two sectors to limit their political clout;<ref name="GG" /><ref name="TEA" /> Lutrillia itself fell within the bounds of the Yarith sector.<ref name="GG" />

This situation persisted through the next few hundred years. Lutrillia was on the borders of the Republic during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], and the world became part of [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn's]] holdings in [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]]. By [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], the Yarith and Anoat sectors were once again considered part of the Javin sector.<ref name="TEA" /> The Lutrillians and their region were spared the atrocities of the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] [[Yuuzhan Vong War|invasion]] of the galaxy in<ref name="GATORW" /> 25 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|ABY]]. In [[137 ABY]], it was part of [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire]].<ref name="TEA" />

==Lutrillians in the galaxy==
===An influential bunch===
{{Quote|Who you calling 'old,' pal?|The Lutrillian Solomahal, to Covah|<ref name="GG" />}}
[[File:Lutrillian.jpg|thumb|right|250px|upright|A sizable number of Lutrillians lived in Cloud City on Bespin.]]
Lutrillians who grew tired of life on their homeworld often left for greener pastures. In fact, it was quite common for Lutrillians to barter passage off their world to pursue adventure and wealth in the greater galaxy. They could be found throughout the Outer Rim, working as entrepreneurs, businessbeings, and government bureaucrats. More adventurous Lutrillians found work as [[Fringer/Legends|fringers]], [[Scoundrel/Legends|scoundrels]], and scouts.<ref name="GATORW" />

The Lutrillians were one of the four most influential species in the Greater Javin, along with Humans, Mugaari, and Nothoiins; the competition between these groups sometimes spilled over into out-and-out rivalry.<ref name="R&T">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20040325adv|text=Rough and Tundra|int=Rough and Tundra}}</ref> Lutrillian emigrants formed colonies on other worlds,<ref name="GATORW" /> and several planets had significant Lutrillian populations. In addition to their homeworld, the beings held a sizable presence on worlds along the Corellian Trade Spine, including Kirtarkin, Gerrenthum, and Ione. In the Lutrillian Cross and [["The Loop" (hyperlane)|the Loop]] that connected to it, Lutrillians were an important component of the population of the swamp world Mijos, where they ran several spaceports.<ref name="GG" /> Some 100,000 to 360,000 Lutrillians called [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]] home, making up about 6% of its population.<ref name="GATORW" /><ref name="TEA" /><ref name="BAT">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20040930bespinmain|text=Bespin: Action Tidings|int=Bespin: Action Tidings}}</ref> Lutrillians were present in smaller numbers on planets such as [[Oseon VII]]<ref name="MF">[[Millennium Falcon (novel)|''Millennium Falcon'']]</ref> and [[Svivren/Legends|Svivren]],<ref name="MJ2" /> and in locations such as [[Horn Station]]<ref name="Incident at Horn Station">{{Tales|2|Incident at Horn Station}}</ref> and [[StarForge Station]].<ref name="PW">{{WEGCite|story=Preparing for War|book=The Far Orbit Project}}</ref>

Several Lutrillians made a name for themselves in the galaxy at large. [[Solomahal/Legends|Solomahal]] was a Republic general during the Clone Wars who headed the Republic defenses on the planet [[Azure/Legends|Azure]]. Although he lost the [[Battle of Azure Spaceport]] and was captured by the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatists]], he managed to destroy an important codebreaker and escape with his life,<ref name="SOTJ" /> actions that made him a hero of the conflict. After the war, he turned to [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] work in the Outer Rim, based himself on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], and lived in hiding from the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]].<ref name="R&T" />

===Late Republic era and beyond===
{{Quote|Kill him, Hardeen! Like the Jedi!|A Lutrillian prisoner, egging on a prison fight|<ref name="Dec" />}}
The Lutrillian [[Maysano/Legends|Maysano]] had a record in a [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] database of criminals; during the Clone Wars, the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Jocasta Nu/Legends|Jocasta Nu]] and [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]] briefly considered the Lutrillian a possible suspect in their search of a thief who had stolen Tano's [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]],<ref name="LL">{{TCW|Lightsaber Lost}}</ref> and Tano viewed his file on another occasion while trying to prevent an [[Assassin/Legends|assassination]] she had [[Farsight/Legends|seen]] in a vision.<ref name="A" />

[[File:LutrillianandUgnaught-JoY.jpg|thumb|left|250px|A Lutrillian and an [[Ugnaught/Legends|Ugnaught]]]]
By a later point in the war, the [[Republic Judiciary Central Detention Center/Legends|Republic Judiciary Central Detention Center]] on Coruscant held a large population of Lutrillian [[Prisoner/Legends|inmates]]. When the Human [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] infiltrated the prison disguised as the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Rako Hardeen/Legends|Rako Hardeen]] to gather intelligence about the activities of a [[Phindian/Legends|Phindian]] [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] named [[Moralo Eval/Legends|Moralo Eval]], the Jedi's presence eventually led to a prisoner riot. One Lutrillian stole a [[Blaster rifle/Legends|blaster rifle]] from a [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone trooper]] guard; although the prisoner was felled by a [[Stun/Legends|stun]] blast from another guard, his actions caused enough chaos for Kenobi, now working alongside Eval and the [[Duros/Legends|Duros]] [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] [[Hunting/Legends|hunter]] [[Cad Bane/Legends|Cad Bane]], to escape the facility.<ref name="Dec" /> The Lutrillians [[Atheloe]] and [[Ownellco/Legends|Ownellco]] were present at [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]] in Mos Eisley the day Obi-Wan Kenobi and Luke Skywalker met Han Solo and Chewbacca<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref><ref name="RG">{{InsiderCite|130|Rogues Gallery|Rogues Gallery: The Unusual Suspects: Who's Who in Mos Eisley}}</ref> in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]].<ref name="TNEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates the events of {{Film|IV}} and {{Film|V}} to [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]] and [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], respectively.</ref> Members of the species visited [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]] on that planet as well.<ref name="TPM 1/2">[[Episode I: The Phantom Menace ½|''Episode I: The Phantom Menace'' ½]]</ref>

Other Lutrillians, in contrast, established themselves in business, from a hospitality specialist on Oseon VII,<ref name="MF" /> to [[Treva Horme]], who worked her way up to become part-owner and head salesbeing for [[Planet Dreams, Incorporated|Planet Dreams, Inc.]], a [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]] firm that constructed vacation homes on unused, habitable worlds in the Greater Javin and even isolated [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroids]].<ref name="R&T" /> After the evacuation of the city<ref name="GG3">[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back'', Second Edition]]</ref> in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]],<ref name="TNEC" /> she relocated with her business partner [[Wiorkettle]] to the [[Oseon asteroid belt]].<ref name="GG3" /> Finally, [[Sawthawne]] was a Lutrillian gangster who operated from Cloud City's [[Port Town (Cloud City)/Legends|Port Town]] district. His presence attracted a band of bounty hunters, scoundrels, and [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] to the area.<ref name="GATORW" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Mos_Eisley_BTS_group_shot.jpg|thumb|right|275px|Two Lutrillian costumes were produced for ''A New Hope''. The only distinction was an ascot worn by one of the two extras.]]
The species name "Lutrillian" was first introduced in the [[1996]] [[West End Games]] [[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game|roleplaying]] supplement [[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back'']]. In the guide, the character Treva Horme was established to be a member of the species.<ref name="GG3" /> In the fall of that year,<ref name="Fall">{{GalaxyCite|12|Around the Galaxy}}</ref> [[Decipher]]'s ''[[Cloud City Limited]]'' set for the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]] [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] Horme to have appeared in the<ref name="CCG">{{CCG|set=Cloud City Limited|cardname=Treva Horme}}</ref> [[1980]] [[original trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']].<ref name="ESB" /> The image used on the card<ref name="CCG" /> depicted the same species that was seen in the background of the cantina scene of the [[1977]] original trilogy film, [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], thereby making ''A New Hope'' mark the Lutrillians new first appearance.<ref name="ANH" />

[[Stuart Freeborn]] designed those characters after costume sketches by [[John Mollo]]; the characters were on set in London during principal photography,<ref name="SWC">''[[Star Wars Chronicles]]''</ref> and they are more prominently featured in an early cut of the sequence, with one of them speaking to an [[Insectoid/Legends|insectoid]] [[Alien/Legends|alien]].<ref name="BTM">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref> During production, the crew referred to the Lutrillians as "The Colonel"<ref name="sw.com">{{SWArchive|url=episode-iv/bts/article/f20030502/index.html|text=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases|int=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases}}</ref> and the "Hare Mouse."<ref name="SWC" /> Although both Lutrillian costumes from ''A New Hope'' are identical save for an ascot worn by one of the two actors,<ref name="MOSW">''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]''</ref> one of these Lutrillians was slated to be named "Ownellco." One of the masks was used again in [[1978]]'s ''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]''.<ref name="sw.com" />
